blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Aligning supply with demand is the quiet engine of any good supply chain. It sounds obvious, but most operational trouble comes from failures of alignment: a plant running flat out while warehouses are full, a warehouse empty while the factory is idle, a customer waiting while inventory sits in the wrong country.

Alignment is not a one-time calculation. It is a rhythm. Every week, planners check what customers are actually ordering against what the company is actually producing, and they adjust: they move stock, shift capacity, and change priorities. Over a year, hundreds of small adjustments produce the steady balance that looks, from the outside, like luck.

The teams that get this right are almost invisible. The ones that do not become very visible — loudly, in complaints, costs, and board meetings.

items.q: According to the text, where does most operational trouble come from?
items.why: "most operational trouble comes from failures of alignment" — o desalinhamento entre oferta e demanda é a causa central.

items.q: How does the text describe alignment?
options: A rhythm of weekly checks and adjustments
A one-time calculation done at year-end
A software product the company installs
A decision made only by the board
items.why: "Alignment is not a one-time calculation. It is a rhythm." — checagem e ajuste semanais.

items.q: What produces the "steady balance that looks, from the outside, like luck"?
items.why: "hundreds of small adjustments produce the steady balance" — o equilíbrio vem da soma de muitos ajustes.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Small weekly adjustments matter more than they seem.
A well-run planning team keeps stock moving to the right place.
If the numbers are set once, the operation will stay balanced.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que alinhamento é ritmo contínuo, não um cálculo único — logo o autor discordaria de "definir uma vez basta".

items.q: The line about teams that "become very visible — loudly, in complaints, costs, and board meetings" suggests that…
options: Visible teams are the best-run teams
Poor alignment draws attention through problems, not praise
Complaints are a normal part of any operation
items.why: Inferência: a visibilidade citada é negativa — surge quando o desalinhamento vira reclamação, custo e pauta de reunião.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie explicando a um novo gerente de planejamento como a reunião semanal funciona. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So this is the meeting people underestimate. Thirty minutes, every Tuesday, same room, same faces. On paper it looks like nothing. In practice, I think it quietly prevents about half of the emergencies we used to have.

Here is what we actually do. We put two numbers side by side: what customers ordered last week, and what the plants produced last week. Then we look for the biggest gaps first — never the small ones. If a line is running flat out but the warehouse is already full, that is a gap. If a factory sits idle while a customer in another country is waiting, that is a gap too.

And then we do three things, always in the same order: we move stock, we shift capacity, and we change priorities. Nothing dramatic — a container rerouted here, a shift added there. It feels almost boring.

The trick is that we adjust every single week. Small corrections, constantly. When you only check the numbers once a month, the gaps grow quietly, and by the time you notice, it is already a crisis. Do this on Tuesday and most of the fires never start.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Sophie, what does the Tuesday meeting quietly prevent?
options: The need to hire more planners
About half of the emergencies they used to have
items.why: "it quietly prevents about half of the emergencies we used to have."

items.q: Which two numbers does the team put side by side?
options: Last year's demand and this year's demand
What customers ordered and what the plants produced
items.why: "what customers ordered last week, and what the plants produced last week."

items.q: In what order does the team act each week?
options: Shift capacity, change priorities, move stock
Move stock, shift capacity, change priorities
Change priorities, move stock, shift capacity
Move stock, change priorities, shift capacity
items.why: "we move stock, we shift capacity, and we change priorities" — sempre nessa ordem.

items.q: Why does Sophie warn against checking the numbers only once a month?
options: The gaps grow quietly and become a crisis before anyone notices
Monthly reports cost more to produce
items.why: Inferência: sem correção frequente, os desvios crescem sem serem vistos e viram crise — por isso o ritmo semanal.

items.q: What does Sophie imply when she says the work "feels almost boring"?
options: The undramatic routine is exactly what keeps problems from exploding
The team should look for more exciting tasks
The meeting is a waste of time
items.why: Inferência: o tom monótono é elogio — pequenas correções previsíveis evitam os incêndios, e é isso que ela valoriza.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The plant was running flat out all week to clear the backlog." Running flat out means…
items.why: Flat out = a todo vapor, no máximo da capacidade.

items.q: "Half the machines sat idle while orders piled up elsewhere." Idle means…
items.why: Idle = ocioso, parado sem uso.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We can add a night shift to raise ___ before the peak season."
items.why: Capacity = capacidade — o quanto a operação consegue produzir.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Planning is a weekly ___, not a single event once a quarter."
items.why: Rhythm = ritmo — a rotina cadenciada de checar e ajustar.

items.q: "Each week we make a small adjustment instead of a big correction." An adjustment is…
options: a minor change to keep things on track
items.why: Adjustment = ajuste, uma pequena mudança para manter o equilíbrio.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de planejamento. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's line up production with what customers actually ordered." To line up with means to…
items.why: Line up with = alinhar, colocar em correspondência — o tema central da lição.

items.q: "When demand jumped, we had to ramp up capacity fast." To ramp up means to…
items.why: Ramp up = aumentar de forma progressiva (o oposto é ramp down).

items.q: "A weekly meeting helps us stay on top of the gaps." To stay on top of means to…
options: keep in control of and up to date with
items.why: Stay on top of = manter sob controle, acompanhar de perto para não deixar acumular.

items.q: "Small corrections now stop a shortage from building up." To build up means to…
items.why: Build up = acumular-se aos poucos — a lição mostra os desvios crescendo em silêncio.

items.q: "Agreeing the plan is easy; the challenge is to follow through every week." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim, executar o que foi combinado — aqui, manter a disciplina semanal.
